reconstruction.scope: Standing Temple of Hercules at Amman: two tall plain segmented shafts with original simplified Corinthian leafy capitals and short broken lintel, four broken uncapped shafts at distinct heights, molded bases/local rubble footings. Low interrupted cella/perimeter masonry, occupied earthen portico mound/graded front approach and a few fallen drums/cornice fragments. Existing shared Corinthian capital/base geometry is adapted without its fluted shaft. No intact cella/roof, restored missing column rows, copied inscription/sculpture atlas or separate hand-of-Hercules artifact. Museum, Roman Temenos, watchtower, sculpture garden and surrounding city remain independent.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Picture/map estimates: two complete columns10.2m above local portico floor, plain shafts with drum seams and original simplified Corinthian caps; four broken shafts5.8/3.7/8.3/2.3m. Joining lintel3.6m between column centers, about0.75m deep above capitals, with broad molded registers/chipped ends. Cella ruins follow rear27x21m extent, interrupted1-2m masonry above local grade; exact inventory/heights/breaks remain approximate. Front portico soil fill supports the bases and slopes to native approach; no hypothetical complete classical stair or full temple restoration.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Retain original pinned standard6m Mapzen hill terrain, paths/water and every independent building. Occupied column bases share a level floor just above sampled footing maxima with individually buried local masonry feet. Only the actual front portico has an authored earthen mound/graded approach; low cella/perimeter wall bottoms/tops follow native grade. No precinct-wide slab, terrain flattening, ground/water cutout or neighboring museum removal. Coarse DEM varies several meters across the main footprint and cannot resolve archaeological paving/mound sections, so foundation depths/thresholds and wall profiles remain visualization estimates.
